name: Russia–NATO
value: Missile, objects in Polish airspace 20 Nov
summary: NATO's Rutte calls the 20 Nov Russian missile incursion into Poland unacceptable; Warsaw has not invoked Article 4
state: A Russian Kh-101 cruise missile and two other objects, believed to be a second missile and a jet-powered drone, came down inside Poland on 20 Nov; Polish F-16s backed by NATO responded (A News). After talks with Prime Minister Tusk in Warsaw on 21 Nov, NATO Secretary General Rutte called the breach dangerous and unacceptable; Poland has not invoked Article 4 but has asked for more NATO forces and air defence (A News; UK Defence Journal). No direct clash or Article 4 request was found, so Watch holds.
for_you: No change for travellers to Poland is indicated; check FCDO travel advice before travel near the Polish–Ukrainian or Polish–Belarusian borders, where airspace restrictions and military activity are more likely.
rubric_hit: Watch: airspace violation (Russian missile and objects in Polish airspace 20 Nov); no Article 4 request or clash

sources.title: A News — Allies stand with Poland after airspace breach by Russia: NATO chief
UK Defence Journal — Russian missile enters NATO airspace, crashes in Poland

why: Direct Russia–NATO confrontation is the most likely path to a European war involving the UK.
drivers: Airspace and drone incursions, sabotage, Baltic incidents, nuclear signalling, Ukraine war spillover.

rubric.alert: Article 4 consultations, a direct military clash, or an attack on NATO territory.
rubric.watch: Airspace/drone violations, sabotage attributed to Russia, or explicit threats against members.
rubric.normal: No notable incidents on NATO territory in the past two weeks.
